note: Our own words for the functions of the firmware that the sources bind, for docs/firmware-interfaces.md (tools/interfaces.py makes the page). For an address: a short name, its group, what the caller hands over and gets back, and the threads our code calls it on. Only what a caller needs is said here; how a function works inside is not (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Writing about the firmware"). Every address belongs to OS 1.7.3.
about: This page lists the functions of the firmware that open-field's own code calls, for OS 1.7.3. For each it says where the function stands, what the caller hands over, what comes back and which thread our code calls it on. It says nothing of how a function works inside: that is not needed to call it, and it is not written down in this repository ([CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md), "Writing about the firmware").
**Every address belongs to one firmware file**, OS 1.7.3. On another version each one has to be found again ([methods](methods.md), "Moving the work to another firmware version").
**How a source binds a function.** Two lines: the function's type, and a name for its address. The type is ours; nothing of the firmware is copied.

**How arguments travel.** The first three go in the registers R0, R1 and R2, the rest on the stack. A result comes back in R0. A function that gives back a structure gets the address for it in P0. The compiler does all of that when the type is right, so a wrong type is a crash: before you bind a function that is not on this page, read how the firmware itself calls it ([methods](methods.md), "Reading a caller before you bind a function").

**The threads.** *The main thread* runs the start-up. *The display thread* draws a frame some sixty times a second; the shared part calls our frame functions from it. *The key thread* hands key presses and knob turns to the mode that is shown. *The audio thread* makes the sound, a block of 64 samples at a time, and must never wait: no log line, no file, no memory asked for there. Where the last column says "ours", it names the threads our code calls the function on today; that it is safe on another thread has not been shown.

log.title: The log
log.about: The unit writes a log into the folder `logs` of its disk. [Methods](methods.md) says how to copy a log off the unit and how to read one.

files.title: Files on the unit's disk
files.about: A path is a C text, counted from the top of the unit's disk, with no slash in front: `user/pk/kit.pack`. There are two families of calls. Use one family for a file from its open to its close.

json.title: JSON values and JSON files
json.about: The firmware keeps its settings as JSON, and so does our code. A JSON value is a small object of 12 bytes in memory the caller provides (our code keeps 16). It owns what it holds: make it with `json_ctor`, give it back with `json_dtor`. What `json_at`, `json_get` and `json_lookup` give back is a reference into another value, not a value of the caller's to destroy. A value has a kind: 0 nothing (null), 1 an integer, 2 an unsigned number, 3 a number with a fraction, 4 a text, 5 true or false, 6 an array, 7 an object. A number read from a file has the kind 2 or 3, never 1: do not test for 1, ask `json_int`.

memory.title: Texts and memory
memory.about: Our code has no library of its own: no `malloc`, no `memcpy`, no division by a variable. What it needs of memory it keeps in its own data, or asks of the firmware with the calls below.

screens.title: Screens, pictures and texts
screens.about: A screen of the firmware is an object with a picture: an SVG text, parsed into a document whose parts can be found by their id, shown, hidden, moved and given a text. Our own screens are made the same way.

keys.title: Keys and the screen that is shown

sounds.title: Sounds, effects and engines
sounds.about: The synth and the drum each keep eight slots. A slot has a record of 52 bytes whose document, the sound as its file holds it, is the JSON value at the record's +8; the synth's eight records start at `0x080235dc`, the drum's at `0x0802377c`. An effect has a type, 0 to 10 for the firmware's own (delay, grid, punch, phone, spring, mother, nitro, cwo, vocoder, terminal, fazer). The firmware keeps two effect objects at a time: index 0 for the instrument that plays, index 1 for the master.

notes.title: Notes and sequencers
notes.about: These play on the instrument the unit is on: the synth or the drum, by the firmware's play mode. A note is a MIDI note number, 0 to 127.

tape.title: The tape's document and its save
tape.about: The firmware keeps the tape's settings as one JSON document, read from the tape's file at a load and written into it at a save. The save runs on the firmware's background worker, the lowest of its threads, which also loads the sounds picked in the unit's list.

disk.title: The disk mode
disk.about: When the unit is a disk on a computer, the firmware builds a tree of folders and files to show. A folder has a behaviour: an object whose first word is a table of functions. The word at +0x10 makes the behaviour of a folder inside it by its name, and the word at +0x14 gives a file object for a file of it by its name; each answers 0 for a name it does not take.

unit.title: The keyboard controller, MIDI out and the restart
unit.about: Calls that reach beyond the firmware's own memory: the keyboard controller, the USB MIDI output, and the restart of the unit.

0x8c053a20.name: log
0x8c053a20.what: Writes one line into the unit's log. `level`: 3 for a line of information, 2 for a warning, 1 for an error. `file`: a text in the form of a source path; the log shows what stands between its last slash and its dot as the line's tag, so `op1f/mypack.cpp` gives the tag `mypack`. A text without a slash and a dot gives a line with no tag. `line`: a number shown in brackets behind the tag. `format` and the values behind it: as `printf` takes them. A line is cut at about 260 characters, the time and the tag counted.
0x8c053a20.thread: Any thread but the audio thread: keep a count there and print it from a frame function. Ours: the main thread at the start, the display thread, the key thread, the tape's background thread.

0x8c051f9c.name: file_size
0x8c051f9c.what: The size of the file at a path, in bytes; -1 when there is no such file. It writes nothing into the log, so it is the way to ask whether a file is there.
0x8c051f9c.thread: Not the audio thread. Ours: the main thread at the start, the display thread, the disk mode's thread.

0x8fc8a9d8.name: file_open
0x8fc8a9d8.what: Opens a file. `mode` is a text as C's `fopen` takes it; our code hands over the firmware's own text for reading, `rb`, which stands at `0x848daec0`. Gives back a descriptor, a small number that may be 0. A negative number means the open failed, and the function has then written a line into the log itself.
0x8fc8a9d8.thread: Not the audio thread. Ours: the main thread at the start and when a screen is made, and the display thread.

0x8fc8a9a8.name: file_read
0x8fc8a9a8.what: Reads `count` items of `size` bytes into the buffer. Gives back the number of items read. The descriptor is the fourth argument, so it travels on the stack.

0x8c0a3630.name: file_seek
0x8c0a3630.what: Goes to a place in a file opened with `file_open`. The offset is 64 bits wide and is handed over as two words, the low one first. `from`: 0 counts from the file's start, 1 from the present place, 2 from the file's end. Gives back the low word of the new place.

0x8c05206c.name: make_folders
0x8c05206c.what: Makes the folders of a path that are missing. Only a part that a slash ends is made: `user/fx/` makes both folders, `user/fx` makes `user` alone.

0x8fcbefb4.name: file_remove
0x8fcbefb4.what: Removes the file at a path. Gives back 0 when the file is gone.

0x8c051e28.name: dir_open
0x8c051e28.what: Opens a folder to list it. The path has no slash at its end. Gives back a handle, or 0 when the folder cannot be opened.
0x8c051e28.thread: Not the audio thread. Ours: the main thread at the start, the disk mode's thread.

0x8c0a4bd0.name: dir_next
0x8c0a4bd0.what: The next entry of a folder opened with `dir_open`, or 0 at the end. The entry's name is the text that starts 11 bytes into what comes back. Do not count on the order of the entries: our code sorts the names itself.

0x8c085ba8.name: json_ctor
0x8c085ba8.what: Makes a value of a kind in the caller's 12 bytes. Kind 0 makes a null, which becomes an array at its first `json_push`.
0x8c085ba8.thread: Not the audio thread. Ours: the main thread at the start, the display thread, the key thread.

0x8c0844e0.name: json_dtor
0x8c0844e0.what: Gives back what a value holds. Call it for every value made with `json_ctor`, and for none that is a reference.

0x8c0534d0.name: json_read_file
0x8c0534d0.what: Reads a JSON file and parses it into a value the caller has made. Not 0 when the file was read and parsed.

0x8c053168.name: json_write_file
0x8c053168.what: Writes a value as a JSON file. The path is a text object of the firmware (`string_ctor` below), not a C text. The file is written under a spare name in the folder `tmp` and then renamed over the target. 0 comes back when that failed: look at the answer, and make the target's folder first.

0x8c084840.name: json_int
0x8c084840.what: A number as an `int`. It takes all three kinds of number. For any other kind it gives back 0 and writes a line into the log.

0x8c084c22.name: json_size
0x8c084c22.what: How many elements an array has. Ask it of an array only.

0x8c084ee0.name: json_at
0x8c084ee0.what: An array's element by its number, from 0: a reference into the array.

0x8c085068.name: json_has
0x8c085068.what: Not 0 when an object has a member of that name.

0x8c084f74.name: json_get
0x8c084f74.what: An object's member by its name: a reference into the object. Our code asks `json_has` first and never asks for a member that is not there.

0x8c085e84.name: json_lookup
0x8c085e84.what: An object's member by its name, as `json_get` gives it; a member that is not there is made, as a null. The way to add a member: look it up, then assign to it.

0x8c0845b8.name: json_assign
0x8c0845b8.what: Gives a value the content of another. The target may be a reference, such as a member got with `json_lookup`.

0x8c085d54.name: json_push
0x8c085d54.what: Puts a copy of a value at an array's end. A null becomes an array at its first push.

0x8c083b1c.name: json_from_int
0x8c083b1c.what: Makes a value an integer (the kind 1).

0x8c083aec.name: json_from_bool
0x8c083aec.what: Makes a value true or false (the kind 5).

0x8c084430.name: json_from_cstr
0x8c084430.what: Makes a value a text (the kind 4), copied from a C text.

0x8c03e434.name: string_ctor
0x8c03e434.what: Makes a text object of the firmware from a C text, in memory the caller provides (our code keeps 48 zeroed bytes for it). A text of up to fifteen characters lives inside the object, and nothing has to be freed afterwards. Our code keeps its paths that short for this reason: `user/op1f.json` fits, `user/lfo/01.json` does not.
0x8c03e434.thread: Not the audio thread. Ours: the main thread at the start, the display thread, the key thread, the disk mode's thread.

0x8fcc7560.name: alloc
0x8fcc7560.what: A block of the firmware's own heap, the one its screens and pictures come from. It never gives back 0: when the heap has no room, the firmware writes an error into the log and stops. So bound what you ask for (our picture maker asks for a megabyte at most) and give every block back with `free` at `0x8fcc6c30`.
0x8fcc7560.thread: Not the audio thread. Ours: the main thread when a screen is made, and the display thread.

0x8fcc6c30.name: free
0x8fcc6c30.what: Gives back a block got with `alloc` at `0x8fcc7560`.

0x8fcc51fc.name: heap_free
0x8fcc51fc.what: How many bytes of such a heap are not in use, by the heap's number.

0x8c040298.name: parse_svg
0x8c040298.what: Parses a picture, an SVG text that a zero byte ends, into a document. Gives back the document, or 0. Hand it only what the firmware's own pictures use: the path commands M, L, H, V, C, S and z in capitals or small letters, and no attribute its own files lack. A path command it does not know makes it hang, and the unit with it.
0x8c040298.thread: Ours: the main thread when a screen is made, and the display thread.

0x8fc26398.name: screen_ctor
0x8fc26398.what: Makes a screen object in memory the caller provides (our code keeps 64 bytes) and registers it under a number. Register a screen once: a number that is taken stops the firmware. In OS 1.7.3 our code uses the numbers 37, 38 and 77, which are free there. Keep a number below 82: the firmware draws the screens in the order of their numbers, and a screen above 82 is drawn over the shutdown countdown. The object's second word is its document: put the parsed picture there. `name` may be 0.

0x8fc25cc0.name: find_node
0x8fc25cc0.what: Finds a part of a screen's picture by its id. With `optional` not 0 it gives back 0 for a part that is not there, and our code always asks that way. The screen must have its document: look at the object's second word before you ask.

0x8c03dbbe.name: apply_matrix
0x8c03dbbe.what: Gives a part of a picture a transform: nine words, each a number with ten bits behind the point, `[a, b, 0, c, d, 0, e, f, 1024]`, for x' = a·x + c·y + e and y' = b·x + d·y + f. Keep the third, sixth and ninth word at 0, 0 and 1024.

0x8fc25abc.name: label_from_node
0x8fc25abc.what: Turns a part of a picture into a label, an object whose text can be set while the unit runs. The part is a placeholder: it gives the label its place and its colour. The label takes the part's place in the document and comes back; keep it, since the id finds it no more. Our code passes 0 for `kind`: the text then starts at the placeholder's left edge.
0x8fc25abc.thread: Ours: the display thread, once for each label.

0x8fc3aa3c.name: label_text
0x8fc3aa3c.what: Sets a label's text from a C text. A text wider than `max_width` pixels is shortened and gets a mark at its end. An empty text hides the label. Send small letters and digits: the firmware's font has the letters at the small letters' codes and its own signs at the capitals'. Each call asks the heap for memory, so set a text only when it changes; setting the text a label already has changes nothing.

0x8fc3820c.name: label_bounds
0x8fc3820c.what: The box of a label's text as it was last laid out: left, right, top and bottom, each a number with ten bits behind the point. It is the box of the shapes without their stroke, so an upright stroke is 0 wide. The box comes back as a structure, by value: bind the function as one that returns the structure, and the compiler hands over the address for it in P0.

0x8c0b2554.name: request_screen
0x8c0b2554.what: Asks the firmware to show the screen the present mode wants now. The firmware does this itself after every key; our code calls it after a change that no key press follows, such as a timer running out. It takes no argument. From the display thread, call it with interrupts masked for the length of the call: the firmware stops when two threads are inside it at once.
0x8c0b2554.thread: Ours: the key thread, and the display thread with interrupts masked.

0x8fc24ca4.name: shift
0x8fc24ca4.what: Not 0 while the shift key is held.
0x8fc24ca4.thread: Ours: the key thread, the display thread.

0x8fc64c68.name: settings_screen_make
0x8fc64c68.what: Makes a screen of the kind the settings rows KEYBOARD, SYSTEM and MIDI show on the right: up to seven lines, a name and a value each, and one set of seven lines that all such screens share. `screen` is a block of 44 bytes from the allocator; `name` is a text in small letters, which the list on the left shows in capitals. The function writes the screen's table into its first word: our code writes a table of its own over it, its name function first and its draw second. Each call empties the seven shared lines, so make a screen once, at the start.
0x8fc64c68.thread: Ours: the main thread at the start.

0x8fc64de0.name: settings_screen_draw
0x8fc64de0.what: Draws the right side of such a screen: the first lines of the shared seven, as many as the word at `screen + 0xc` says, in the unit's own letters and colours, with the line the word at `screen + 8` names drawn as the chosen one. `context` is what the firmware hands a screen's draw: pass it on as it came.
0x8fc64de0.thread: Ours: the display thread, from our own screen's draw.

0x8fc64c2c.name: settings_line_name
0x8fc64c2c.what: Sets the name on line `line` (0 to 6) of the seven shared lines: a text in small letters, at most 31 characters, shown in capitals. `screen` is not read: the lines are the same for every such screen, so write them right before the draw of the screen they are meant for.
0x8fc64c2c.thread: Ours: the display thread and the key thread.

0x8fc64c08.name: settings_line_value
0x8fc64c08.what: Sets the value on line `line` (0 to 6) of the seven shared lines, as `settings_line_name` sets the name.
0x8fc64c08.thread: Ours: the display thread and the key thread.

0x8c0b68b0.name: knob_item_top
0x8c0b68b0.what: Sets the highest value of one of the unit's knob items, the 32-byte objects the settings' items and line pickers are made of, to `top` whole steps, and holds the item's value to it. KEYBOARD, SYSTEM and MIDI keep their line picker in the row at `row + 4`, with the number of lines less one as its top. The firmware stops when the top is below the item's lowest value.

0x8c0d44b0.name: keyboard_chosen
0x8c0d44b0.what: The settings screen lists its rows on the left; a row is an object whose first word is the address of its table of functions, which the firmware calls on the key thread. This is KEYBOARD's function for its row being chosen (`row`: the row). It writes the row's own three lines into the shared seven, sets the number of lines in the row (the word at `row + 0x2c`) and in its screen, and sets the top of the row's line picker. The firmware calls it through the row's table; our code calls it first from its own function in that word of the table.

0x8c0d4d0c.name: system_chosen
0x8c0d4d0c.what: The same for SYSTEM, with its six lines.

0x8c0d484c.name: midi_chosen
0x8c0d484c.what: The same for MIDI, with its five lines.

0x8c0d45ce.name: keyboard_red
0x8c0d45ce.what: The settings row KEYBOARD's function for a turn of the red knob on line `line` of its row (`row`). `amount` is the turn as the firmware hands it, a float: pass it on as it came. Hand it only the row's own lines, 0 to 2.

0x8c0d5018.name: system_red
0x8c0d5018.what: The same for SYSTEM: only its own lines, 0 to 5.

0x8c0d49d0.name: midi_red
0x8c0d49d0.what: The same for MIDI: only its own lines, 0 to 4.

0x8c053a50.name: assert
0x8c053a50.what: Writes `message` into the log, then stops the unit for good: it never comes back. Our code puts an endless loop after it all the same.
0x8c053a50.thread: Ours: the main thread at the start.

0x8c051f88.name: rename
0x8c051f88.what: Renames a file: `from` and `to` are paths as `file_size` takes them. Both must be counted from the top of the disk or both begin with a slash: one of each stops the unit. Not 0 when the rename was made. The file system behind it replaces a target that is there in one step.
0x8c051f88.thread: Not the audio thread. Ours: the display thread, the main task when it handles a SysEx message.

0x8c052054.name: is_folder
0x8c052054.what: Not 0 when the path opens as a folder, written without a slash at its end. It opens the folder and closes it again.

0x8c0a4730.name: free_space
0x8c0a4730.what: The free bytes of the file system the path names, as one number of 64 bits (R1:R0); -1 on a failure. Our code hands over `/yaffs2`, the text the firmware's own callers hand over.
0x8c0a4730.thread: Ours: the main task when it handles a SysEx message.

0x8fcba988.name: open
0x8fcba988.what: The second family: the calls of the firmware's file class. Opens a file and gives back a handle, or -1 with a line in the log. `mode` is one of four texts, compared as texts: `rb`, `ab`, `r+b` and `w+b`, which makes the file anew. Any other mode is refused with a line. A path that begins with a slash is taken from the device's root; any other is counted from the top of the unit's disk.
0x8fcba988.thread: Not the audio thread. Ours: the display thread, the disk mode's thread, the main task when it handles a SysEx message.

0x8fcba954.name: read
0x8fcba954.what: Reads `count` items of `size` bytes from a file opened with `open`. Gives back the number of items read. The handle is the fourth argument, so it travels on the stack.

0x8fcba8c0.name: write
0x8fcba8c0.what: Writes `count` items of `size` bytes into a file opened with `open`. Gives back the number of items written, or 0 with the line `write error` in the log. The handle is the fourth argument.

0x8c084748.name: json_cstring
0x8c084748.what: The characters of a text value (the kind 4): the value's own, not a copy, good while the value lives and is not changed. A value of any other kind stops the unit: ask the kind first.
0x8c084748.thread: Not the audio thread. Ours: the display thread, the key thread, the main task, the firmware's background worker.

0x8c0828e0.name: json_read_raw
0x8c0828e0.what: The parse under `json_read_file`: it reads a JSON text that is already in memory into a value. `a` is the firmware's JSON reader, an object on the caller's stack; `path` is not a path but a text object of the firmware that holds the whole text to parse; `value` is the value to fill; the firmware's own callers hand 1 for `flag`. Not 0 when the text was parsed. Our code calls it only in place of the firmware's own call, with the arguments that call came with.
0x8c0828e0.thread: Ours: in place of the firmware's own call in the synth's read of a preset, on the firmware's background worker.

0x8d4e63bc.name: new
0x8d4e63bc.what: A block of `bytes` from the firmware's heap: the C++ `new` of the firmware, which `alloc` calls. As `alloc`, it never gives back 0: with no room the firmware writes an error into the log and stops. Give the block back with `free` at `0x8d4e63cc`.
0x8d4e63bc.thread: Not the audio thread. Ours: the main thread at the start, the disk mode's thread.

0x8d4e63cc.name: free
0x8d4e63cc.what: Gives back a block of the firmware's heap: one from `new`, or the text of a firmware text object that holds sixteen characters or more.

0x8fc261fc.name: screens
0x8fc261fc.what: The table of the firmware's screens by their numbers: a word a number, the screen object or 0 for a number no screen has. A screen's document is the word at its +4, 0 until the firmware has loaded it. Our code reads only the numbers 1 to 85.

0x8fc273f0.name: screen_of
0x8fc273f0.what: The number of the screen of an effect's type, 0 to 10. For any other type it writes a line into the log and gives back 86.

0x8fc274ac.name: engine_screen
0x8fc274ac.what: The number of the screen of a synth engine's type. For a type that has no screen it writes a line into the log and gives back 86.

0x8c0dd2cc.name: draw_char
0x8c0dd2cc.what: Draws one character of the firmware's small bitmap font into a frame buffer, at the cursor: the two words at `0x840148b0` (x) and `0x840148b4` (y). Every pixel of the character's cell is written, the character's in white and the rest in black. The cursor's x moves on by the character's width and one. A byte 0x80 to 0xbf draws nothing; any other character outside 0x20 to 0x7e is drawn as `?`. A character that does not fit before x = 480 is not drawn, and the cursor stays. Our code sets the cursor before a text and puts it back after.

0x8fca6940.name: tick
0x8fca6940.what: The firmware's work of a frame before the draw, called by the display thread's frame loop. It takes one argument, the object the loop hands over, and gives nothing back. Our code calls it in place of the loop's own call, with the registers as they came.

0x8fc27678.name: draw
0x8fc27678.what: The whole draw of a frame: every screen that is shown, into the frame buffer the loop hands over, its one argument. It gives nothing back. Our code calls it in place of the loop's own call, with the registers as they came.

0x8d4f6c3c.name: synth_put
0x8d4f6c3c.what: Puts a sound on a synth slot: `record` is the slot's record, `slot` its number, 0 to 7, and `json` the sound's document, which is assigned to the record's. With `flag` 0 the firmware then keeps of the record's document only the members it knows. Last it sets the name the screen shows for the slot; a `slot` outside 0 to 7 sets no name. Nothing comes back.
0x8d4f6c3c.thread: Ours: the firmware's background worker, in place of its own call when a sound is loaded from the unit's list.

0x8d4f6748.name: drum_put
0x8d4f6748.what: The same for a drum slot. With `flag` 0, a document the firmware's check refuses is written as an error into the log.

0x8d4f3b9c.name: set_params
0x8d4f3b9c.what: Writes an effect's eight knob words into a slot's document, as the member `fx_params`: each word is a value shifted left by sixteen, and the value is what goes in. Then the record is marked to be written. `record` is the slot's record.

0x8d4f3c24.name: set_active
0x8d4f3c24.what: Writes whether a slot's effect is on into the slot's document, as the member `fx_active`, and marks the record to be written. `record` is the slot's record.
0x8d4f3c24.thread: Ours: the key thread, the display thread.

0x8d4f689c.name: knob_set
0x8d4f689c.what: Writes a synth slot's eight knob words into its document, as the member `knobs`, each a value shifted left by sixteen, and marks the record to be written. The words of the sampler's sounds are taken another way: some of them are written as other members.

0x8d504320.name: on_synth
0x8d504320.what: Sets the byte that says whether the effect of synth slot `slot` plays. Only that byte: nothing is written into the slot's document.
0x8d504320.thread: Ours: the display thread, and in place of the firmware's own call when a slot's sound is applied.

0x8d5042f0.name: on_drum
0x8d5042f0.what: The same for a drum slot.

0x8d5042c0.name: on_master
0x8d5042c0.what: The same for the master's effect.

0x8d50424c.name: master_on
0x8d50424c.what: Whether the master's effect plays: the byte `on_master` sets.
0x8d50424c.thread: Ours: in place of the firmware's own call when the master is saved.

0x8c0bb684.name: master_pick
0x8c0bb684.what: The mixer's pick of the master's effect: the function in the word +0x28 of the mixer's controller's table (the word at `0x8400f2cc`). `controller` is the mixer's controller, `id` the id of the effect's row in the catalog's list `fx_types`. Our code calls it with the controller as it came.
0x8c0bb684.thread: Ours: the key thread, in place of the firmware's own call.

0x8f011068.name: factory
0x8f011068.what: Makes an effect object of a type, 0 to 10, for an index, 0 or 1, and gives it back; 0, with a line in the log, for any other type or index. Each index has one room: an object made for an index is made in the place of the one made before for it. The object's first word is its table of functions.
0x8f011068.thread: Ours: in place of the firmware's own call, on whatever thread that call runs.

0x8d505390.name: build
0x8d505390.what: Makes the effect object of `index` anew for a type: it clears the index's word, makes the object with `factory`, starts it and puts it in the word. A type the factory refuses stops the unit.

0x8d4fee88.name: user_sounds
0x8d4fee88.what: The number of user sounds the unit holds, synth and drum together. It stops the unit when the synth's or the drum's total is 0, as it is before the firmware's first count: our code reads the two totals first and calls it only when both are not 0.
0x8d4fee88.thread: Ours: the display thread, with interrupts masked.

0x8fca2220.name: classic
0x8fca2220.what: Not 0 when the unit holds the file `content/op1.classic`. The first call looks on the disk; every call after gives back what it found.
0x8fca2220.thread: Not the audio thread. Ours: the display thread.

0x8f007d68.name: note_record
0x8f007d68.what: The note a key plays: `key`, the key's number, and `velocity` become a record of four words, the MIDI note first and the velocity second. The note is 53 and the key, and on the synth twelve times its keyboard octave more. The record comes back as a structure, by value: bind the function as one that returns the structure, and the compiler hands over the address for it in P0.
0x8f007d68.thread: Ours: the key thread, the audio thread or a MIDI handler's thread, when a key reaches a pack's sequencer.

0x8f008388.name: note_on
0x8f008388.what: Begins `note` at `velocity` on the instrument the unit is on, as a key does, and sends it out over MIDI. A `velocity` of -1 is taken as 127. A note above 127 stops the unit. `octave` counts on the drum only. `target` is where the MIDI goes, 0 for the unit's own settings; with `no_midi` not 0 nothing is sent. Our code hands 0 for `third`, `fourth`, `octave` and `target`.
0x8f008388.thread: Ours: from a pack's sequencer calls: the sequencer thread, the key thread, the audio thread, a MIDI handler's thread.

0x8f008518.name: note_off
0x8f008518.what: Ends `note` on the instrument the unit is on and sends the end out over MIDI, unless `no_midi` is not 0; `target` as for `note_on`. A note outside 0 to 127 is passed over. While the firmware holds its notes, as with a sustain pedal, the end waits until they are let go. Our code hands 64 for `velocity` and 0 for `third`, `fourth` and `target`.

0x8f008ba8.name: bend
0x8f008ba8.what: Sets the pitch of the synth's voices that play `note`. `pitch` is a pitch word as the firmware's table of pitches holds them. It works on the synth's voices: our code calls it only while the unit is on the synth.

0x8fc97844.name: player_word
0x8fc97844.what: The address of the word that holds the sequencer player of the instrument the unit is on: the drum's while the unit is on the drum, else the synth's. A player is an object whose first word is its table of functions.
0x8fc97844.thread: Ours: the key thread, or the main thread at the start.

0x8fc978fc.name: current_player
0x8fc978fc.what: The player in that word: the object, or 0.

0x8fc9e818.name: restart_allowed
0x8fc9e818.what: Not 0 when the unit's clock settings let the sequencers' count be set back now, as the firmware's own sequencers ask before they set it back at a first key.

0x8fc9e868.name: restart
0x8fc9e868.what: Sets the sequencers' count back to its start. It takes nothing and gives nothing back. Ask `restart_allowed` first.

0x8fc681a0.name: overlay_match
0x8fc681a0.what: The matcher of the notice "sequencer off": the function in the word at `0x848d8668`, its table's. `overlay` is the notice's object and `screen` a screen's number. Our code answers in its place for the packs' page and hands it every other call with the arguments as they came.
0x8fc681a0.thread: Ours: in place of the firmware's own call.

0x8d4f2b80.name: tape_root
0x8d4f2b80.what: The tape's document: a JSON value at a fixed place, the same every call. The unit stops when the document is null.
0x8d4f2b80.thread: Not the audio thread. Ours: the firmware's background worker, the key thread, the main task.

0x8d4f24dc.name: tape_set
0x8d4f24dc.what: Sets a member of one of the firmware's documents to a copy of `value`, under the documents' lock, and marks that document changed. `db` picks the document: 2 is the tape's, the one `tape_root` gives. `key` is the member's name. It waits for the lock as long as it takes, so it waits while a tape's file is read or written. Gives back 1.
0x8d4f24dc.thread: Not the audio thread. Ours: the firmware's background worker, in the tape's save.

0x8c0c1dd0.name: tape_saver
0x8c0c1dd0.what: The tape's saver: an object of the firmware's, made at the first call and the same at every call after. Hand it to `notify` to have the tape saved.

0x8fca1ed2.name: notify
0x8fca1ed2.what: Marks a saver to save and wakes the background worker, which then saves. It does not wait.

0x8fcacea0.name: root_child
0x8fcacea0.what: The root folder's behaviour's maker of a folder inside it: the function in the word at `0x8490fc4c`, the root behaviour's +0x10. `behaviour` is the root behaviour, `name` the folder's name; it gives back the behaviour of that folder, or 0. Our code calls it for every name that is not its own, with the arguments as they came.
0x8fcacea0.thread: Ours: the disk mode's thread, in place of the firmware's own call.

0x8fcaeb10.name: make_folder
0x8fcaeb10.what: Makes a folder of the disk mode's tree inside `parent` and gives it back. The folder's behaviour comes from the parent's behaviour, its word at +0x10. It gives back 0 with a line in the log for a name the parent already has, or when the behaviour gives none.

0x8fcaed68.name: add_file
0x8fcaed68.what: Adds a file to a folder of the disk mode's tree and gives back its node, or 0 when the folder's behaviour gives no file object for the name (its word at +0x14). An empty name stops the unit.

0x8fcbabb8.name: fs_file_ctor
0x8fcbabb8.what: Makes the firmware's file object for a file on the disk in memory the caller provides, 64 bytes from `new`: the object the disk mode reads and writes a file through. The path is copied into a text object of the firmware at the object's +4, and the file is not open yet. The object's first word is its table of twelve functions.

0x8c0567f0.name: kb_request
0x8c0567f0.what: Sends a request to the keyboard controller and waits for its answer. `link` is the controller's link, at `0x8497d844`; `type` the request; `payload` and `bytes` what goes with it, 0 and 0 for none. The answer is copied whole into `answer`, the type at its byte 2, the length at byte 3 and the payload from byte 4; it may be copied there even after the wait is over, so keep the buffer out of the stack. `timeout_ms` bounds the wait. Not 0 when the answer came in time; 0 when it did not, or when four requests are already waiting.
0x8c0567f0.thread: Ours: the main thread at the start.

0x8d4e5cb8.name: midi_out
0x8d4e5cb8.what: Hands USB MIDI packets, four bytes each, to the MIDI output: `index` is the port, `packets` the packets, `bytes` their length in bytes. In some states of the USB connection nothing is sent and nothing is said, and it gives nothing back: our code looks at the output's room and at the USB mode first, and sends only in the mode 1.
0x8d4e5cb8.thread: Ours: the main task when it handles a SysEx message.

0x8c0df868.name: restart
0x8c0df868.what: Asks for a restart: writes the line `got request to enter DFU mode` into the log, keeps `code` and the time of the call, and comes back. `delay_ms` later the firmware's main loop shuts the unit down and starts it again; the delay is kept in sixteen bits. `code` picks what starts next. Our code hands 20, and the unit comes back into the OS; 20 is also the code the firmware's own automatic power-off writes. The firmware's MIDI request to enter its update mode hands other codes.
0x8c0df868.thread: Ours: the main task when it handles a SysEx message, the display thread.
